analysis.summary_en: To assess the benefits and harms of thymosin-ɑ1 therapy in people with chronic hepatitis B. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluated thymosin-α1 at any dose, route of administration, or formulation type, in people with chronic hepatitis B regardless of age, sex, or ethnicity. We identified no ongoing trials. Reasons for downgrading were mainly due to study limitations, including overall high or some concerns for risk of bias; imprecision of the pooled effect estimates (including wide or very wide confidence intervals crossing the line of no effect, and small participant numbers); and inconsistency due to substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 74%). Follow-ups ranged from six months to five years after the end of treatment (median: 12 months).

title: Extremely low diagnostic yield of routine hepatitis B and human immunodeficiency virus screening among incarcerated adults treated for hepatitis C in Western Australia.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Routine testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is recommended prior to initiating direct‐acting antiviral (DAA) therapy for hepatitis C virus (HCV) in Australian prisons. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic yield of HBV and HIV screening among incarcerated adults treated for HCV.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We evaluated the diagnostic yield of HBV and HIV screening among 713 incarcerated adults commencing DAA therapy across multiple Western Australian prisons between 2017 and 2025. The cohort had a mean age of 34.8 years and was predominantly male (81%).
analysis.methods: HBV and HIV screening outcomes were available for all participants. The study involved routine testing for HBV and HIV among incarcerated adults initiating DAA therapy for HCV.
analysis.main_results: Only one (0.14%) participant tested positive for hepatitis B surface antigen and none for HIV. A further 12% had serological evidence of past HBV exposure.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings confirm an extremely low yield of universal pre‐treatment HBV/HIV screening in this setting. The study represents one of the largest contemporary evaluations of HBV and HIV screening outcomes among incarcerated individuals receiving DAA therapy in Australia.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform the need for alternative strategies to identify HBV infection in incarcerated populations. Parallel testing strategies may streamline care and support hepatitis C elimination efforts in custodial settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the diagnostic yield of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) screening among 713 incarcerated adults in Western Australia who were treated for hepatitis C virus (HCV) with direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy between 2017 and 2025. The results showed that only 0.14% of participants tested positive for HBV, and none for HIV, with an additional 12% having evidence of past HBV exposure. These findings confirm the extremely low yield of universal pre-treatment HBV/HIV screening in this setting, highlighting the need for alternative strategies to identify HBV infection in incarcerated populations. The study contributes to the understanding of screening practices in custodial settings and supports the development of more efficient care models for HCV treatment.

analysis.summary_en: Abstract Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) afflicts approximately 254 million people worldwide and is responsible for more than one million deaths annually. The supplied evidence does not clearly state the study design, setting, or study population. In a cell model of chronic HBV infection, both siR@HM NPs and TPAT@HM NPs achieved targeted delivery to infected hepatocytes. Critically, sequential administration yielded superior antiviral efficacy compared with concurrent administration or either monotherapy, leading to substantial reduction in HBsAg, HBeAg, HBV DNA, cccDNA, and pgRNA levels. In the first step, HM-coated lipid nanoparticles encapsulating siRNA (siR@HM NPs) enable virus to neutralize and hepatocyte targeted delivery via surface viral receptors, achieving efficient gene silencing. Intrahepatic persistence of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), the episomal transcriptional template of hepatitis B virus (HBV), sustains chronic replication, blunts the efficacy of antiviral therapy, and precipitates virological relapse once treatment is discontinued. This bionic platform integrates time-programmed virus targeting, RNA interference, and photothermal ablation.

title: Complete Genome Sequencing of Occult Hepatitis B Virus in Hemodialysis Patients Reveals Subgenotype D2 and Immune Escape Mutations in Bangladesh.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study is aimed at characterizing complete HBV genomes from maintenance HD patients with OBI in Bangladesh to elucidate genetic features, mutational patterns, and clinical implications.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Serum samples from two HBsAg-negative HD patients were screened by ELISA and quantitative PCR.
analysis.methods: Viral DNA was amplified by PCR across four overlapping open reading frames (ORFs) and sequenced on the Illumina platform.
analysis.main_results: Full-length genomes (3182 bp) were successfully sequenced and phylogenetic analysis showed both HBV genomes clustered within Genotype D, Subgenotype D2, and subtype ayw3, consistent with previously reported Bangladeshi HBV genomes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Several nonsynonymous mutations were also detected in polymerase, though none were potentially associated with antiviral resistance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings demonstrate the persistence of OBI in HD patients and provide an initial indication of the need for genomic surveillance to monitor immune-escape mutations and improve HBV diagnostic strategies in endemic regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Antigenicity and hydrophilicity profiles of HBsAg and its major hydrophilic region remained largely conserved.

analysis.summary_en: This study is aimed at characterizing complete HBV genomes from maintenance HD patients with OBI in Bangladesh to elucidate genetic features, mutational patterns, and clinical implications. Serum samples from two HBsAg-negative HD patients were screened by ELISA and quantitative PCR. Viral DNA was amplified by PCR across four overlapping open reading frames (ORFs) and sequenced on the Illumina platform. Full-length genomes (3182 bp) were successfully sequenced and phylogenetic analysis showed both HBV genomes clustered within Genotype D, Subgenotype D2, and subtype ayw3, consistent with previously reported Bangladeshi HBV genomes. Several nonsynonymous mutations were also detected in polymerase, though none were potentially associated with antiviral resistance. These findings demonstrate the persistence of OBI in HD patients and provide an initial indication of the need for genomic surveillance to monitor immune-escape mutations and improve HBV diagnostic strategies in endemic regions. Antigenicity and hydrophilicity profiles of HBsAg and its major hydrophilic region remained largely conserved.

title: Mathematical modeling of HBV-HDV transmission with superinfection: The role of vaccination and liver transplantation in disease dynamics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection can substantially worsen the clinical outcomes of individuals infected with hepatitis B virus (HBV), making the prevention of HBV infection and the management of severe HBV–HDV cases important public-health priorities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study introduces a novel mathematical model for Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and D virus (HDV) transmission, incorporating vaccination and liver transplantation as disease control strategies.
analysis.methods: In contrast to models that allow direct HDV infection or general coinfection pathways, the proposed model assumes that HDV occurs only through superinfection among individuals already infected with HBV.
analysis.main_results: Model analysis reveals the existence and stability of the disease-free equilibrium, which exists and is asymptotically stable if the basic reproduction number (R0) is less than one, and becomes unstable if it exceeds one.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Two types of endemic equilibria are identified when R0 > 1, corresponding to the absence and presence of HDV infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings indicate that vaccination is essential for reducing transmission, whereas liver transplantation remains important for mitigating severe disease burden; thus, coordinated use of preventive and clinical interventions is needed for effective HBV–HDV control.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Continuation analysis using MatCont reveals the existence of two branching points that govern the transition of stability between these equilibria, highlighting the conditions under which HDV emerges and persists.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a novel mathematical model for the transmission dynamics of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and D virus (HDV), focusing on superinfection as the mechanism for HDV acquisition. The model incorporates vaccination and liver transplantation as key interventions. It identifies the disease-free equilibrium and two types of endemic equilibria based on the basic reproduction number (R0). The analysis shows that vaccination coverage and efficacy are critical in reducing R0, while liver transplantation affects outbreak size and timing. The findings emphasize the importance of combining preventive and clinical strategies for effective HBV–HDV control. The study's results are grounded in mathematical modeling and sensitivity analysis, providing insights into disease dynamics and intervention effectiveness. However, the model's assumptions and the lack of empirical data limit the strength of the conclusions.

title: The Impact of HCC Surveillance on Tumor Features and Receipt of Curative Therapy: A Focus on Chronic Hepatitis B and MASLD.

analysis.research_question_and_background: As hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) etiologies shift from viral to non-viral, many at-risk patients lack surveillance in real-world practice. This study characterizes the clinical features and receipt of curative therapy in HCC patients with and without surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at National Taiwan University Hospital (2015–2025). Patients newly diagnosed with HCC who had not undergone regular surveillance (n = 50) were compared with a consecutive surveillance-diagnosed cohort (n = 100).
analysis.methods: Methods included a retrospective cohort study at National Taiwan University Hospital (2015–2025) comparing patients with and without surveillance. Subgroup analyses were performed in patients with chronic hepatitis B and MASLD.
analysis.main_results: Non-surveillance patients had higher baseline liver enzymes and alpha-fetoprotein levels, larger tumors, higher rates of multifocal tumors, and more frequent vascular invasion. Multivariable analysis identified surveillance as a strong independent predictor of receiving curative therapy (odds ratio [OR]: 17.78; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.56–56.88, p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: HCC surveillance was associated with earlier stage at diagnosis and independently predicted receipt of curative therapy; higher BMI was an additional predictor in the HBV subgroup.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the importance of HCC surveillance in improving early detection and curative therapy rates, particularly in patients with chronic hepatitis B and MASLD.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on retrospective data, which may introduce bias and limit the strength of causal inferences. However, the evidence is strong due to the clear association between surveillance and curative therapy receipt.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of HCC surveillance on tumor features and receipt of curative therapy in patients with chronic hepatitis B and MASLD. It highlights that non-surveillance patients present with more advanced disease and lower rates of curative therapy. title: Identification and validation of oxidative stress-related immune signatures in Hepatitis B Virus associated acute liver failure based on WGCNA and machine learning.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Acute liver failure (ALF) is a serious clinical disease. Immune infiltration and oxidative stress (OS) play an important role in ALF, but the combination of oxidative stress and immune infiltration in ALF has not been explored.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were performed on ALF and control samples in the GSE96851 dataset to obtain DE-OS-MGs. Candidate OS-IM-associated signature genes were mined using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and support vector machine (SVM) machine learning. Finally, OS-IM-related signature genes were obtained by expression analysis and ROC validation.
analysis.methods: Single gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), TF-miRNA-mRNA network construction and drug prediction were also performed for OS-IM-related signature genes.
analysis.main_results: Differential analysis identified a total of 3580 DEGs in ALF and control samples, and differential analysis of immune cells yielded 15 immune cell species that were significantly different between the two groups. After WGCNA analysis, 1134 key module genes were screened. Then, 3580 DEGs, 855 OS-related genes, and 1134 key module genes were intersected, resulting in a total of 89 DE-OS-MGs. The expression levels and ROC analysis of the 5 genes were validated in the GSE96851 and GSE120652 datasets, and 4 genes (CLU, APOH, AMBP, and GPX8) were used as biomarkers (OS-IM-related signature genes) for subsequent analysis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as providing a new idea and theoretical basis for the therapeutic diagnosis of ALF.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a new idea and theoretical basis for the therapeutic diagnosis of ALF.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations or evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to explore the role of oxidative stress and immune infiltration in acute liver failure (ALF) associated with hepatitis B virus. The researchers performed differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) on ALF and control samples from the GSE96851 dataset to identify DE-OS-MGs. Candidate OS-IM-related signature genes were mined using LASSO and SVM machine learning, and further validated through expression analysis and ROC analysis. The results identified 4 genes (CLU, APOH, AMBP, and GPX8) as potential biomarkers for ALF. These genes were associated with metabolic processes, and a miRNA-mRNA network was constructed. The study suggests that combining immune infiltration and oxidative stress analysis could offer new insights into the diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for ALF. However, the evidence does not report specific limitations or the strength of the findings.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Switching from Entecavir to Tenofovir Alafenamide for Chronic Hepatitis B Patients with Low-Level Viremia.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Clinical data on the efficacy and safety of tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients with suboptimal response to entecavir (ETV) are limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study was designed to investigate the efficacy and safety of switching to TAF in CHB patients with low-level viremia (LLV). CHB patients with LLV who received ETV treatment for more than 52 weeks were divided into TAF group (n = 104) and ETV group (n = 395).
analysis.methods: Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to adjust for baseline differences in age between the two groups. The outcomes included complete virological response (CVR) at weeks 12 and 24, normalization rates of aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and renal function and blood lipid levels.
analysis.main_results: Compared with the ETV group, the TAF group had significantly higher rates of CVR at week 12 and week 24 in both the raw cohort and the PSM cohort (all P < 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Switching to TAF may be beneficial for patients with LLV after prolonged ETV therapy, as it is associated with a significantly higher rate of CVR.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that switching to TAF could improve virological outcomes in CHB patients with LLV who have been on prolonged ETV therapy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study used propensity score matching to adjust for baseline differences, but the evidence is limited to a single cohort and does not include long-term follow-up data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the efficacy and safety of switching from entecavir (ETV) to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients with low-level viremia (LLV). The research was motivated by the limited clinical data on TAF in this patient group. A total of 499 patients were divided into TAF group (n = 104) and ETV group (n = 395). Propensity score matching was used to adjust for age differences. The outcomes included complete virological response (CVR) at weeks 12 and 24, normalization of ALT and AST levels, and assessments of renal function and blood lipid levels. The results showed that the TAF group had significantly higher CVR rates at both time points compared to the ETV group. The authors concluded that switching to TAF may be beneficial for patients with LLV after prolonged ETV therapy. The study's findings could inform treatment strategies for CHB patients with LLV, but the evidence is limited to a single cohort and lacks long-term follow-up data.

title: Machine Learning Model for Predicting Hepatocellular Carcinoma Development in Patients With Hepatitis B Virus-Related Cirrhosis Receiving Antiviral Therapy.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Few prediction models have been specifically designed to evaluate the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in patients with chronic hepatitis B and cirrhosis. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-based prediction model to assess the risk of developing HCC in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis undergoing nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We included 1592 patients with HBV-related cirrhosis who had received entecavir, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, or tenofovir alafenamide for at least 1 year. Patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio into derivation or validation groups, and the prediction model was developed using the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm.
analysis.methods: The proposed machine learning model for predicting development of HCC exhibited good predictive performance in patients with HBV-related cirrhosis undergoing NA therapy.
analysis.main_results: The cumulative incidence of HCC for all patients at 5, 8, and 10 years was 15.2%, 22.7%, and 25.7%, respectively. In the validation group, the AUROCs of the ML-HCC model ranged from 0.79 to 0.80 over 3 to 10 years, outperforming extant models including APA-B, PLAN-B, PAGE-B, mPAGE-B, REACH-B, and CU-HCC (AUROCs: 0.61-0.73, p < 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our ML-HCC model incorporated six parameters: serum albumin and platelet count at treatment initiation, and age, platelet count, serum aspartate transaminase, and serum AFP after 1 year of NA therapy. The model demonstrated superior predictive performance compared to existing models, suggesting a novel approach for risk assessment in HBV-related cirrhosis patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted surveillance and risk stratification strategies for patients with HBV-related cirrhosis undergoing antiviral therapy. This model may improve early detection and management of HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on a single dataset and may have limited generalizability. The model's performance was validated against existing models, but further testing in diverse populations is needed. The evidence strength is moderate due to the study's design and potential limitations in external validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a machine learning-based model to predict hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in patients with HBV-related cirrhosis undergoing antiviral therapy. The model demonstrated AUROCs of 0.79 to 0.80, outperforming existing models. title: Longitudinal Adherence Trajectories of First-Line Nucleotide Analogues among US Older Adults with Chronic Hepatitis B.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The effectiveness of first-line nucleotide analogs (NAs) for managing chronic hepatitis B (CHB) depends heavily on treatment adherence; however, evidence on longitudinal adherence patterns is limited, especially in older adults.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cohort study involved continuously enrolled Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥ 65 years with CHB from 2014-2019.
analysis.methods: Monthly adherence was evaluated using proportion of days covered for incident NAs users, specifically entecavir (ETV), tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF), and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF). Longitudinal adherence patterns were analyzed using group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) over a 12-month follow-up. The variation in adherence trajectories across first-line NAs was examined using a multinomial logistic regression model, adjusted for baseline covariates.
analysis.main_results: The study cohort comprised 3,317 older adults with CHB, with a mean age of 72.6 years, and 57.85% were men. The GBTM identified three long-term adherence patterns: consistently adherent (56.89%), gradual decline (24.78%), and rapid decline (18.33%). The consistently adherent patients varied across the individual NAs (ETV = 52.21%, TDF = 57.39%, and TAF = 71.06%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The multinomial logistic model found that patients on TAF had 0.41 times lower odds of being rapid decliners (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.34-0.49) and 0.45 times lower odds of being gradual decliners (95%CI: 0.39-0.53), compared to ETV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Understanding these long-term adherence patterns can help in developing targeted interventions to improve CHB care in older adults.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated longitudinal adherence trajectories of first-line nucleotide analogs (NAs) among older adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in the US. The research aimed to address the limited evidence on adherence patterns in this population, as adherence significantly impacts the effectiveness of NA treatment. A retrospective cohort study was conducted on continuously enrolled Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥ 65 years with CHB from 2014 to 2019. Monthly adherence was assessed using the proportion of days covered for incident users of entecavir (ETV), tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF), and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF). Group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) identified three adherence patterns: consistently adherent (56.89%), gradual decline (24.78%), and rapid decline (18.33%). The multinomial logistic regression model revealed that TAF was associated with lower odds of declining adherence compared to ETV. These findings highlight the importance of understanding adherence patterns to improve CHB management in older adults. The study provides valuable insights into treatment adherence but does not report limitations.

title: Hepatitis B virus reactivation risk in haploidentical versus matched donor transplantation: Impact of universal prophylaxis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus reactivation is a serious complication of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation, particularly in endemic regions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Patients with HBsAg-negative/anti-HBc-positive serology represent an intermediate-risk group due to occult hepatitis B virus infection.
analysis.methods: A retrospective cohort study of 165 adult hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients with HBsAg-negative/anti-HBc-positive status was conducted at China Medical University Hospital, Taiwan from 2010-2025. Univariable associations, clinical outcomes, and temporal patterns were analyzed.
analysis.main_results: Pre-prophylaxis, haploidentical recipients had higher reactivation rates (11.2% vs. 2.9%), but this did not reach statistical significance due to the small number of events (Odds ratio: 4.31; 95% CI: 0.67-37.55; p = 0.279). In the univariable analyses, hepatitis B virus reactivation was associated with chronic graft-versus-host disease (p = 0.001) and donor anti-HBs negativity (p = 0.001), with a median time to reactivation of 8.2 months.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The incidence of hepatitis B virus reactivation was compared between the pre-prophylaxis (2010-February 2021) and post-policy implementation (March 2021-2025) periods.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This study evaluated hepatitis B virus reactivation risk in haploidentical versus matched donor hematopoietic cell transplantation and assessed the effectiveness of Taiwan's universal prophylaxis policy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: In this cohort, haploidentical hematopoietic cell transplantation with post-transplant cyclophosphamide was associated with a higher observed rate of hepatitis B virus reactivation than matched donor transplantation in HBsAg-negative/anti-HBc-positive recipients, although this difference was not statistically significant.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the risk of hepatitis B virus reactivation in haploidentical versus matched donor hematopoietic cell transplantation in HBsAg-negative/anti-HBc-positive recipients. It evaluates the impact of Taiwan's universal prophylaxis policy on reactivation rates. The research highlights that haploidentical transplantation was associated with a higher observed reactivation rate, though this difference was not statistically significant. The study also identifies factors such as chronic graft-versus-host disease and donor anti-HBs negativity as associated with reactivation. The findings suggest that further research is needed to determine the effectiveness of prophylaxis strategies in reducing reactivation risk. The study's limitations include the lack of statistical significance and the potential for confounding factors.

title: Hepatitis B vaccine-induced immunity among hill tribe and stateless children in northern Thailand

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health problem of suboptimal hepatitis B vaccine-induced immunity in marginalized hill tribe and stateless children in northern Thailand, where vaccination began in 1992. It aimed to quantify seroprotection differences between fully and partially vaccinated children and to identify factors linked to the absence of anti-HBs antibodies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case–control study was conducted in villages of Mae Fah Luang District, Chiang Rai Province, enrolling hill tribe and stateless children aged five years. Cases were children with no prior, delayed, or incomplete hepatitis B vaccination, while controls were those who were completely vaccinated.
analysis.methods: A questionnaire was administered and 3 mL blood samples were collected for qualitative and quantitative detection of hepatitis B biomarkers. Logistic regression was used to detect factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs.
analysis.main_results: The overall anti-HBs prevalence was 59.3%, with 55.3% detected in both fully vaccinated and incompletely vaccinated children (2 children positive for anti-HBc among the fully vaccinated).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the low seroprotection rate as undesirable and highlighted maternal Yao ethnicity and low birth weight as strong predictors of anti-HBs absence. They concluded that an effective assessment program is needed to monitor vaccine-induced immunity in these populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings indicate that targeted vaccination programs and post-vaccination serosurveillance are warranted for hill tribe and stateless children in northern Thailand to improve hepatitis B immunity and reduce transmission risk.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported vaccination status limit causal inference and may underestimate true seroprotection gaps. The evidence is moderate due to potential selection bias and unmeasured confounders.

analysis.summary_en: This case–control study in northern Thailand evaluated hepatitis B vaccine-induced immunity among hill tribe and stateless children aged five years, comparing fully and partially vaccinated groups. Using questionnaires and blood biomarker testing, the authors found an overall anti-HBs prevalence of 59.3%, with no meaningful difference between fully and incompletely vaccinated children. Logistic regression identified low birth weight, maternal Yao ethnicity, maternal Christianity, and paternal age 30–39 years as factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs. The authors concluded that vaccine-induced immune responses remain suboptimal and called for enhanced monitoring and targeted immunization programs in these marginalized populations.

title: Hepatitis B and C Knowledge, Testing Uptake, and Vaccination Coverage Among Men Aged 15-49 in Nepal: A Nationally Representative Analysis of the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess knowledge of hepatitis B and C, its sociodemographic determinants, and testing uptake among men aged 15–49 in Nepal to support elimination efforts. The background highlights Nepal's commitment to addressing viral hepatitis as a public health threat and the need to understand knowledge, testing and vaccination for potential elimination in this age group.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional nationally representative survey was conducted using the men’s recode dataset from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS). The study focused on males aged 15–49 years across Nepal, with data analyzed by province, wealth quintile, age group, place of residence, and ecological zone.
analysis.methods: The study used survey-weighted linear and logistic regression models to analyze factors associated with adequate hepatitis knowledge. The survey-weighted estimation was adjusted for primary sampling unit, strata, and sampling weights using the svydesign function in R. The model's discrimination ability was assessed using the receiver operating curve and area under the curve (ROC-AUC), while the concentration index evaluated equity in knowledge distribution by wealth quintile.
analysis.main_results: After applying survey weights, the prevalence of adequate hepatitis knowledge varied significantly by province, with Gandaki at 81.5% (95% CI: 76.5–86.5) and Sudurpashchim at 76.3% (72.1–80.5) being among the higher provinces, while Madhesh had the lowest at 58.0% (53.7–62.2). There was a clear wealth gradient, with 65.3% (61.8–68.9) in the poorest quintile and 82.0% (79.2–84.9) in the richest quintile having adequate knowledge. The model showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.703) and moderate explanatory power (McFadden pseudo-R2 = 0.087), with a concentration index of −0.030 indicating a slight pro-poor distribution of knowledge.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that knowledge disparities among Nepali men are influenced by education, geography, and internet access. The study's novelty lies in its focus on male-specific knowledge and its contribution to understanding the factors affecting health literacy in this demographic.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform targeted public health interventions to improve hepatitis knowledge in provinces with lower coverage, such as Madhesh and Karnali, and highlight the need for gender-disaggregated surveillance to monitor progress toward hepatitis elimination goals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study has limitations due to the lack of hepatitis testing or vaccination status data among male respondents, which precludes analysis of testing uptake and vaccination coverage. Despite this, the evidence is moderate in strength, supported by survey-weighted regression models and cross-validation procedures.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed hepatitis B and C knowledge among Nepali men aged 15–49 using data from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey. It found significant provincial and wealth-related disparities in knowledge, with higher levels in Gandaki and Sudurpashchim and lower in Madhesh. Education, age, internet use, and ecological zone were identified as key predictors of adequate knowledge. The study highlights the need for improved gender-disaggregated surveillance and targeted interventions to address health literacy gaps. However, the lack of testing and vaccination data limits the analysis of uptake and coverage, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Association of alanine aminotransferase flares with hepatitis B surface antigen loss and clinical outcomes in treated and untreated patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection: A US retrospective cohort study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Previous research has demonstrated the clinical significance of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) flares; however, studies have mostly been in Asian countries or populations, and it remains unclear whether ALT flares during treatment are associated with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss and long-term adverse clinical outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Retrospective study using the Optum de-identified electronic health record dataset (2012-2019). At least one ALT flare was experienced by 364 patients (2.5%) in the untreated cohort, 84 (3.7%) in the treatment initiation cohort, and 22 (1.4%) in the discontinuation cohort.
analysis.methods: Marginal structural models estimated the associations between ALT flares and outcomes, accounting for time-varying confounding; adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals were reported. A Cox proportional hazards regression model was used to assess risk factors for flares.
analysis.main_results: 14,328 patients were included in the untreated cohort; of these, 2298 (16.0%) initiated and 1541 (10.7%) subsequently discontinued treatment. Flares in the untreated group were associated with spontaneous HBsAg loss and with an increased risk of hepatic decompensation, hospitalization, and death. Flares after treatment initiation were associated with HBsAg and HBeAg loss but not with adverse clinical outcomes investigated.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: ALT flares in untreated patients were associated with virologic and adverse clinical outcomes; no association with adverse clinical outcomes was observed in patients who initiated treatment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform surveillance and risk assessment strategies for patients with chronic hepatitis B, particularly in understanding the role of ALT flares in predicting HBsAg loss and adverse clinical outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on electronic health records, which may introduce bias and limit the ability to establish causality. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between alanine aminotransferase (ALT) flares and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in the United States. It evaluates whether ALT flares are linked to HBsAg loss and adverse outcomes in both treated and untreated populations. The study uses a retrospective cohort design based on the Optum electronic health record dataset from 2012 to 2019. Results show that ALT flares in untreated patients are associated with spontaneous HBsAg loss and increased risk of hepatic decompensation, hospitalization, and death. In contrast, flares after treatment initiation are linked to HBsAg and HBeAg loss but not to adverse clinical outcomes. The authors conclude that ALT flares have different implications depending on treatment status, highlighting the need for further research to understand their role in HBV management. The study's limitations include its observational design and potential biases inherent in electronic health record data, which may affect the strength of the conclusions.

title: Hepatitis B Virus: Epidemiology, Prophylaxis, Therapy, Clinical Outcomes, and Novel Therapeutic Directions

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a worldwide health concern that infects nearly 254 million people globally and causes more than 1 million deaths annually. The highest prevalence is seen in sub-Saharan Africa and the Western Pacific region.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This review summarizes the epidemiology, prevention, current therapies, clinical outcomes, and emerging therapeutic advances in HBV infection, highlighting ongoing efforts toward achieving a functional cure and global HBV elimination.
analysis.methods: The management of chronic hepatitis B virus infection predominantly depends on nucleoside analogs, including entecavir, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, and tenofovir alafenamide, as well as pegylated interferon alfa.
analysis.main_results: Cirrhosis, liver failure, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are reported as leading complications of chronic HBV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Current prevention strategies include universal vaccination, perinatal prophylaxis with hepatitis B immune globulin, and maternal antiviral therapy in pregnant women with high viral load.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Vaccination has significantly reduced HBV seroprevalence and complications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: However, incomplete vaccination of newborns continues to be a major obstacle to elimination of the disease.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides an overview of the epidemiology, prevention, and treatment of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, emphasizing its global impact and the challenges in its elimination. The study highlights the major complications of chronic HBV, including cirrhosis, liver failure, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It outlines current therapeutic approaches, such as nucleoside analogs and pegylated interferon, which effectively suppress viral replication but rarely achieve a functional cure. The review also discusses prevention strategies, including universal vaccination and perinatal prophylaxis, and notes that incomplete vaccination of newborns remains a significant barrier to disease elimination. The findings underscore the need for improved vaccination coverage and the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting different stages of the viral life cycle.

title: Application of the Information-Knowledge-Attitude-Practice Model in Breastfeeding Management for Pregnant Women with High Hepatitis B Virus Load.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of the Information–Knowledge–Attitude–Practice (IKAP) model in breastfeeding management for pregnant women with high hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA loads (≥ 2 × 105 IU/mL).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective quasi-experimental study enrolled 136 eligible women between January 2023 and October 2023. Based on compliance, 68 who received the full IKAP-based intervention were assigned to the experimental group, and 68 who received routine health education served as controls.
analysis.methods: The experimental group received systematic, individualised IKAP-model education from the second trimester through 12 months postpartum, progressing through information, knowledge, attitude and practice stages. The control group received routine education (eg, prenatal classes, outpatient consultations).
analysis.main_results: The exclusive breastfeeding rate at 42 days was significantly higher in the intervention group (85.29%) than in the control group (67.65%) (absolute risk difference = 17.64%, relative risk = 1.26, p 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The phased IKAP model demonstrated superior outcomes compared with conventional education, safely increasing exclusive breastfeeding rates by approximately 17% and enhancing feeding confidence in high-risk mothers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide an effective and scalable framework for real-world application in supporting pregnant women with high hepatitis B virus loads.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Despite limitations, such as a non-randomised, single-centre design, it provides an effective and scalable framework for real-world application in supporting this special population.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of the Information–Knowledge–Attitude–Practice (IKAP) model in breastfeeding management for pregnant women with high hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA loads (≥ 2 × 105 IU/mL). A prospective quasi-experimental design was used, enrolling 136 women between January 2023 and October 2023, with 68 assigned to the experimental group receiving systematic, individualised IKAP education and 68 to the control group receiving routine health education. The results showed that the intervention group had a significantly higher exclusive breastfeeding rate at 42 days postpartum (85.29%) compared to the control group (67.65%), with an absolute risk difference of 17.64% and a relative risk of 1.26 (p 0.05). The authors concluded that the phased IKAP model demonstrated superior outcomes compared with conventional education, safely increasing exclusive breastfeeding rates by approximately 17% and enhancing feeding confidence in high-risk mothers. The study's non-randomised, single-centre design limits its generalisability, but it provides an effective and scalable framework for real-world application in supporting this special population.

title: Serum Interleukin-6 Concentrations in Patients with Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C Virus Infections: A Comparative Cross-sectional Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are major causes of chronic liver disease and are associated with complex host immune and inflammatory responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A comparative cross-sectional study was conducted among 38 patients with viral hepatitis, including 7 patients with HBV infection and 31 patients with HCV infection.
analysis.methods: IL-6 levels were compared between the two groups using an appropriate independent-group statistical test.
analysis.main_results: However, the difference was not statistically significant (Welch's t-test, P = 0.297).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The standardised effect size was moderate (Cohen's d = −0.59).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings do not provide sufficient evidence of a differential serum IL-6 response between HBV and HCV infections in this study.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Further studies with larger sample sizes and additional clinical, biochemical, and virological parameters are warranted to clarify the inflammatory cytokine profiles associated with HBV and HCV infections.

analysis.summary_en: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are major causes of chronic liver disease and are associated with complex host immune and inflammatory responses. A comparative cross-sectional study was conducted among 38 patients with viral hepatitis, including 7 patients with HBV infection and 31 patients with HCV infection. IL-6 levels were compared between the two groups using an appropriate independent-group statistical test. However, the difference was not statistically significant (Welch's t-test, P = 0.297). The standardised effect size was moderate (Cohen's d = −0.59). These findings do not provide sufficient evidence of a differential serum IL-6 response between HBV and HCV infections in this study. Further studies with larger sample sizes and additional clinical, biochemical, and virological parameters are warranted to clarify the inflammatory cytokine profiles associated with HBV and HCV infections.

title: Cytokine signature behind occult hepatitis B virus infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a serious public health threat and one of the leading causes of acute, chronic and occult hepatitis (OBI).
analysis.study_design_and_population: As controls, 37 healthy donors with the absence of viral hepatitis markers, HIV, and somatic diseases were selected from the same initial cohort.
analysis.methods: Immune mediators (cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors) in blood plasma were measured with the MAGPIX multiplex analysis.
analysis.main_results: We found high levels IL-10 and growth factors (EGF, FLT-3 L, TGFα, G-CSF, M-CSF, VEGF) in OBI patients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: ROC and decision tree analysis indicates that several cytokines hold diagnostic potential as biomarkers for OBI.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: ROC analysis indicates that M-CSF, FLT-3 L, G-CSF, EGF, and TGFα possess diagnostic potential as biomarkers for OBI.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The role of FLT-3 L appear dual, mediating hepatoprotection while simultaneously contributing to fibrotic progression.

analysis.summary_en: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a serious public health threat and one of the leading causes of acute, chronic and occult hepatitis (OBI). As controls, 37 healthy donors with the absence of viral hepatitis markers, HIV, and somatic diseases were selected from the same initial cohort. Immune mediators (cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors) in blood plasma were measured with the MAGPIX multiplex analysis. We found high levels IL-10 and growth factors (EGF, FLT-3 L, TGFα, G-CSF, M-CSF, VEGF) in OBI patients. ROC and decision tree analysis indicates that several cytokines hold diagnostic potential as biomarkers for OBI. ROC analysis indicates that M-CSF, FLT-3 L, G-CSF, EGF, and TGFα possess diagnostic potential as biomarkers for OBI. The role of FLT-3 L appear dual, mediating hepatoprotection while simultaneously contributing to fibrotic progression.

title: A Ganoderma lucidum Polysaccharide-Modified Nanoadjuvant Elicits Potent Cellular Immunity for Hepatitis B Vaccine

analysis.research_question_and_background: Aluminum-adjuvanted hepatitis B vaccines effectively prevent primary HBV infection but predominantly favor humoral immunity and have limited capacity to induce strong cellular responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: C57BL/6 mice were immunized intramuscularly with PBS, HBsAg, HBsAg + Aluminum, HBsAg@HNP, or HBsAg@GHNP6 on Days 0, 14, and 28.
analysis.methods: Cationic PEG-PCL/DOTAP hybrid nanoparticles (HNPs) were surface-modified with Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide (GLP) at different mass ratios and characterized by particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, and transmission electron microscopy. Antigen uptake, RAW264.7 cell viability, MHC II expression, and TLR2/4-associated TNF-α secretion were evaluated in vitro. HBsAg-specific antibodies, splenocyte activation, proliferation, and cytokine secretion were assessed.
analysis.main_results: GHNP6 showed suitable physicochemical properties, acceptable cytocompatibility at concentrations up to 10 μg·mL−1, and efficient model-antigen uptake. GHNP increased MHC II expression in RAW264.7 cells, and TLR2/4 inhibition reduced nanoparticle-associated TNF-α secretion, supporting involvement of these pathways in immune activation. In vivo, HBsAg@GHNP6 induced robust HBsAg-specific IgG responses and a higher IgG2a/IgG1 ratio than HBsAg@HNP and HBsAg + Aluminum. It also produced the highest splenocyte proliferation after HBsAg restimulation, with lower IL-6 secretion than HBsAg + Aluminum and moderately increased IFN-γ compared with PBS and free HBsAg.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: GHNP integrates nanoparticle-assisted antigen delivery with GLP-mediated immunomodulation and represents a promising strategy for enhancing cellular immune responses while maintaining humoral immunity in HBsAg vaccination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that GHNP could improve the quality of immune responses in hepatitis B vaccination, potentially leading to better protection against both acute and chronic HBV infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro and in vivo experiments using mice, which may not fully represent human immune responses. The evidence is moderate as it is based on experimental models rather than clinical trials.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to improve the immune response of hepatitis B vaccines by developing a Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide-modified hybrid nanoparticle adjuvant (GHNP). The researchers evaluated the physicochemical properties and immunomodulatory effects of GHNP in vitro and in vivo using C57BL/6 mice. Results showed that GHNP enhanced MHC II expression and induced robust HBsAg-specific IgG responses with a higher IgG2a/IgG1 ratio compared to other adjuvants. It also promoted splenocyte proliferation and increased IFN-γ secretion. The authors concluded that GHNP represents a promising strategy for enhancing cellular immunity while maintaining humoral immunity in HBV vaccination. However, the study is limited to experimental models, and the evidence is moderate.

title: Biological interpretation of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis in determining interferon treatment duration

analysis.scope_and_question: The recent identification of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis as independent predictors of extended interferon therapy provides a valuable clinical framework, yet the biological mechanisms underlying these associations require further elucidation.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The supplied evidence does not clearly state the review method, databases, eligibility process, or evidence base.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: In this opinion review, we interpret these factors not merely as statistical covariates but as pathological surrogates for the virus-host equilibrium.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: We advocate shifting future predictive modeling from binary clinical definitions to a granular integration of viral kinetics and histological morphology to refine precision medicine in chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Consequently, treatment durations exceeding 48 weeks may be required, at least in part, to overcome these profound immunological and structural barriers.

analysis.summary_en: The recent identification of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis as independent predictors of extended interferon therapy provides a valuable clinical framework, yet the biological mechanisms underlying these associations require further elucidation. The supplied evidence does not clearly state the review method, databases, eligibility process, or evidence base. In this opinion review, we interpret these factors not merely as statistical covariates but as pathological surrogates for the virus-host equilibrium. We advocate shifting future predictive modeling from binary clinical definitions to a granular integration of viral kinetics and histological morphology to refine precision medicine in chronic hepatitis B. Consequently, treatment durations exceeding 48 weeks may be required, at least in part, to overcome these profound immunological and structural barriers.

analysis.summary_en: Among the study population, the most common potential risk factors identified were body piercing (46.6%), tobacco consumption (40.4%), and injection drug use (40%). This cross-sectional study aimed to assess the prevalence of HBV among Rohingya refugees admitted to a tertiary care hospital. Methods This cross-sectional study conducted in the Department of Medicine, Cox’s Bazar Medical College Hospital from August 2018 to January 2019. Results The mean age of study patients was 44.96 ± 15.62 (SD) years, with a slight female predominance (51.6% female vs. Conclusion In this study, seropositivity for hepatitis B virus was observed in 3.1% that needs to be addressed and treated properly. Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a critical public health challenge globally, with particular concern for vulnerable populations like Rohingya refugee or forcibly displaced Myanmar nationals (FDMNs) residing in Cox’s Bazar refugee camps. Appropriate strategic measures are advised to prevent further transmission.

title: From mechanisms to practice: risk management and multidisciplinary decision-making for systemic treatment-related liver injury in HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma

analysis.scope_and_question: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related death globally, with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection as the predominant risk factor.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review summarizes the pathophysiological mechanisms of treatment-related liver injury in HBV-related HCC, analyzes the hepatotoxic profiles of tyrosine kinase inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, combination regimens and emerging agents, and proposes a structured clinical management framework including pretreatment risk assessment, prophylaxis, monitoring, differential diagnosis and severity-based interventions supported by multidisciplinary care.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Systemic therapies including tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), and ICI-antiangiogenic combinations have revolutionized advanced HCC treatment. However, treatment-induced liver injury is a major concern, especially in HBV-related HCC patients with pre-existing inflammation, fibrosis, and cirrhosis, which raises risks of treatment interruption, impaired efficacy, and acute liver failure.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review also highlights key knowledge gaps and future research directions, including predictive biomarkers, personalized risk stratification and proactive safety evaluation of new drugs.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Liver injury arises from direct cytotoxicity, immune-mediated hepatitis, vascular damage, and HBV reactivation.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on the risk management and multidisciplinary decision-making for systemic treatment-related liver injury in HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma. It outlines the pathophysiological mechanisms of liver injury, including direct cytotoxicity, immune-mediated hepatitis, vascular damage, and HBV reactivation. The review highlights the hepatotoxic profiles of various therapies, such as tyrosine kinase inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and combination regimens, and proposes a clinical management framework involving pretreatment risk assessment, prophylaxis, monitoring, and severity-based interventions. Despite the advancements in systemic therapies for advanced HCC, treatment-induced liver injury remains a significant concern, particularly in patients with pre-existing HBV-related inflammation, fibrosis, and cirrhosis. The review identifies key knowledge gaps, such as the need for predictive biomarkers, personalized risk stratification, and proactive safety evaluation of new drugs, which are critical for future research and clinical practice.

title: Stopping is only the beginning: Sequential immune therapy after Nucleos(t)ide analogue withdrawal in chronic hepatitis B.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to explore the potential of sequential immune therapy following nucleos(t)ide analogue withdrawal in managing chronic hepatitis B, addressing the challenge of viral rebound and immune reconstitution.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted as a clinical trial involving patients with chronic hepatitis B who had previously undergone nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy. Participants were followed over time to assess the outcomes of sequential immune therapy.
analysis.methods: The study employed sequential immune therapy protocols, including the use of interferon and other immunomodulatory agents, following nucleos(t)ide analogue withdrawal. Outcomes were defined based on virological and immunological markers.
analysis.main_results: The study observed that sequential immune therapy significantly reduced viral load in some patients and improved immune responses, although not all participants achieved sustained virological suppression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that sequential immune therapy may offer a viable strategy for managing chronic hepatitis B post-treatment, highlighting its potential as a novel approach.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform future treatment strategies for chronic hepatitis B, particularly in managing viral rebound and enhancing immune responses post-antiviral therapy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are based on a limited sample size and may not be generalizable to all patient populations, suggesting a moderate level of evidence for the effectiveness of sequential immune therapy.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the effectiveness of sequential immune therapy following nucleos(t)ide analogue withdrawal in managing chronic hepatitis B. The research aimed to address the issue of viral rebound and immune reconstitution after treatment cessation. The study involved a clinical trial with patients who had previously undergone nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy, and the methods included the use of interferon and immunomodulatory agents. Results showed that sequential immune therapy reduced viral load and improved immune responses in some patients, though not all achieved sustained suppression. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that sequential immune therapy may be a novel approach for managing chronic hepatitis B. The study's implications suggest potential applications in treatment strategies for post-antiviral management. However, the limited sample size and possible lack of generalizability indicate a moderate level of evidence for the observed outcomes.

title: Prevalence and Distribution of Hepatitis B Virus in Patients with SARS-CoV-2: Exploring Co-infection Impacts on Clinical Outcomes and Immune Response

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the impacts of co-infection with Hepatitis B virus and SARS-CoV-2 on clinical outcomes and immune response. The background highlights the interaction between SARS-CoV-2 and chronic viral infections during the COVID-19 pandemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Criminal Evidence, College of Science, University of Hillah, Babylon Iraq, involving 100 patients with proven SARS-CoV-2 and HBV co-infection, 100 patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection alone, and 50 healthy controls aged 10-65.
analysis.methods: Laboratory and immunological markers were measured in patient blood samples. The study spanned from March to August 2024.
analysis.main_results: The COVID + HBV group had a 15.0% death rate, compared to 8.0% for the COVID-19 alone group and 0% for the control group. Both COVID-19 groups experienced higher hospitalization, oxygen consumption, and critical care unit hospitalizations than the control group. The COVID + HBV group showed the lowest immune response, with poorer anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG, IgM, and T-cell activity and a higher rate of breakthrough infections.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that HBV co-infection significantly worsens the clinical outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 infection, likely due to poorer immune responses and higher liver inflammation and dysfunction.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that HBV co-infection may be a critical factor in the severity of SARS-CoV-2 outcomes, highlighting the need for targeted surveillance and management strategies in co-infected populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the specific setting in Babylon, Iraq, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature and potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the effects of co-infection with Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and SARS-CoV-2 on clinical outcomes and immune response. Conducted in Babylon, Iraq, from March to August 2024, it compared 100 co-infected patients, 100 with SARS-CoV-2 alone, and 50 healthy controls. Results showed that the co-infected group had higher hospitalization rates, ICU admissions, and mortality compared to the other groups. They also exhibited lower immune responses and higher breakthrough infections. The authors concluded that HBV co-infection exacerbates the severity of SARS-CoV-2 outcomes, likely due to immune and liver dysfunction. The study's findings have implications for understanding co-infection dynamics and improving clinical management. However, the cross-sectional design and limited geographic scope may affect the generalizability of the results, resulting in moderate confidence in the evidence.
